section_summary: This section comprises press clippings, consular despatches, interdepartmental correspondence, and cross-reference records from 1935 (along with a 1947 State Department charge slip) concerning second-generation Japanese Americans (Nisei) residing, studying, or working in Japan, as well as broader U.S.-Japan educational and cultural exchanges. Key items document the cultural and economic adaptation of Nisei in Tokyo, including female performers introducing American jazz dance, a group of young Californians studying chick sexing in Nagoya to fill U.S. agricultural labor shortages, and survey data on Nisei living conditions and national loyalty. The records reflect ongoing administrative coordination between the Department of State, the Department of Labor, and the War Department regarding Japanese American immigration, technical training, and educational exchange initiatives.

subfiles.about: The concluding portion of an article discussing the economic difficulties, citizenship, national loyalty, and social status of Japanese Americans in both the United States and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Article on Nisei: economic discrimination and exclusion in the US have driven hundreds to Japan, where some groups treat them as Japanese; urges Japanese to respect their American identity and Americans to remove racial barriers.
subfiles.title: Article on the Role and Status of Second-Generation Japanese Americans

subfiles.about: A feature newspaper article profiling four American-born Japanese female performers introducing American jazz, tap, torch singing, and Hawaiian hula to Tokyo audiences.
subfiles.summary: Japan Times & Mail article profiles four Nisei women performers in Tokyo, Fumiko Kawabata, Helen Honda, Betty Inada and Helen Sumida, describing their careers and cultural adjustment.
subfiles.title: They Provide Torch Songs, High Kicks Or The Hula: Second Generation Girls Introducing American Dance

subfiles.about: An internal Department of State charge slip documenting the checkout of decimal file 894.42711.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for file 894.42711, dated July 23, 1947, noting R. E. Barber.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip for File 894.42711

subfiles.about: A consular despatch reporting the arrival in Nagoya of four Japanese American youths from California to study chick sexing at a local specialized training school.
subfiles.from: Charles H. Stephan, American Vice Consul, Nagoya, Japan
subfiles.summary: Nagoya Despatch 23: four American-born Japanese youths from California trained three months at the Nagoya Sexers' Association school to return in January 1936 as chick sexers, as Japanese experts are barred as laborers.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 23 from Nagoya: American-Born Japanese Study Chick Sexing

subfiles.about: A transmittal note from the Secretary of State forwarding a copy of Nagoya Despatch No. 23 concerning chick sexing to the Secretary of Labor.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Secretary of Labor Nagoya Despatch 23 of September 9, 1935 on American-born Japanese studying chick sexing (894.42711/3).
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Nagoya Despatch No. 23 to the Secretary of Labor

subfiles.about: A letter from the Immigration and Naturalization Service acknowledging receipt of Nagoya Despatch No. 23 on chick sexing.
subfiles.from: Henry B. Hazard, Acting Deputy Commissioner, Immigration and Naturalization Service, Department of Labor
subfiles.summary: Immigration Service's Hazard acknowledges receipt of Nagoya Despatch 23; page 251 is an unexecuted carbon copy.
subfiles.title: Letter from Immigration and Naturalization Service Acknowledging Receipt of Nagoya Despatch No. 23
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D. C.

subfiles.about: A War Department routing slip transmitting a Japan Advertiser newspaper clipping summarizing a survey of second-generation Japanese residing in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Military Intelligence routes the Japan Advertiser article 'Nippon Is Verdict': a survey of about 1,000 Tokyo Nisei found language difficulty, rigid society and lower living standards, with nearly 99 percent intending to return to the US or Hawaii.
subfiles.title: War Department Routing Slip and Clipping: 'Nippon Is Verdict'
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet recording correspondence from the Institute of Pacific Relations regarding Japanese graduate exchange students in the United States.
subfiles.from: Bruno Lasker, American Council, Institute of Pacific Relations
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Bruno Lasker's August 9, 1935 letter on fewer Japanese graduate students in the US and Takayanagi's exchange plan (811.42794/66).
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Japanese Exchange Students in the United States
